title: Auth/API 401 & 429 debugging scratchpad (follow-up)
content:
Summary:
- Follow-up scratchpad capturing additional repro attempts and notes. Still seeing intermittent 401 -> 429 pattern. Added more commands and checks and updated next-steps after pinging SRE.

Recent actions (2026-03-04 to 2026-03-05):
- 2026-03-04: SRE confirmed an auth-cache tweak was rolled at 2026-03-02 14:00; they surfaced a spike of cache-miss errors during the deploy window.
- 2026-03-04 11:20: collected traces for sample x-request-ids (rwd-abc123, rwd-def456) and shared with SRE in RS-1234.
- 2026-03-05: did region comparison (us vs eu) and saw higher 401 frequency in eu cluster during my short test.

Commands tried (additional):
- Curl with explicit Host/Region header to force eur cluster routing (for repro):
  API_KEY=redacted
  curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
    -H "Host: eu.api.redwood.ai" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-1.1","prompt":"ping","max_tokens":1}'

- Rapid rotate script (simulate partial-rollout/rotation):
  for k in $(seq 1 5); do 
    KEY=rotated_key_$k; 
    curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-1.1","prompt":"rot","max_tokens":1}'; sleep 0.1; done

More output snippets (interesting):
- 401 with backend error tag in headers:
  HTTP/2 401
  date: Thu, 04 Mar 2026 11:23:12 GMT
  content-type: application/json
  x-request-id: rwd-ghi789
  x-auth-backend: cache-miss

  {"error":"unauthorized","message":"Invalid API key or key revoked"}

- 401 with rate-limit-ish header present (suspect incorrect downstream mapping):
  HTTP/2 401
  date: Thu, 04 Mar 2026 11:23:20 GMT
  content-type: application/json
  x-request-id: rwd-jkl012
  x-rate-limit-remaining: 0

  {"error":"unauthorized","message":"Invalid API key or key revoked"}

Observations update:
- SRE confirms cache-miss spikes during the 2026-03-02 deploy; hypothesis 1 (auth cache eviction / sync lag) strengthened.
- The presence of x-auth-backend: cache-miss header on some 401s is notable — suggests the auth service intentionally marks a missing key as unauthorized rather than proxying to primary DB. Could be a performance optimization that backfired during deploy.
- eu cluster shows higher incidence in quick tests — possibly deploy sequence or config drift.

Updated hypotheses (short):
- Primary: auth cache eviction during deploy caused transient cache-miss -> 401. Combined with burst retries from clients, rate-limiter consumed tokens -> 429.
- Secondary: partial key rollout + regional routing differences exacerbated the window.

Immediate asks to SRE/infra (added):
- [ ] Add metric for auth-service cache-miss rate per region and per deploy id.
- [ ] Change auth-service behavior: on cache-miss, proxy to DB instead of returning 401 immediately (or at least emit different error code for easier debugging).
- [ ] Backfill deploy rollout timeline and which regions were updated when.

Mitigations and temporary best-practices for support: 
- Recommend support rotate keys for impacted customers as stopgap (worked in some cases).
- If customers see 401s, ask them to retry with exponential backoff and capture x-request-id.
- Add guidance to Status page that short-lived 401s may occur during deploys and to contact support with x-request-id.

Next steps (personal):
- [ ] Draft a short runbook for support on how to triage 401->429 reports (include commands above).
- [ ] Work with SRE to run a controlled canary with disabled cache-return-401 behavior to confirm fix.
- [ ] If SRE changes behavior, re-run load test to ensure 401s disappear and only 429s remain when rate limits hit.

References / breadcrumbs:
- Linear RS-1234 (ticket updated with traces).
- Slack: thread in #eng-sre with trace screenshots.

If this doc is stale, check the original: users/auth-api-401-429-debug-scratchpad-lena-2026-03-04.json (older).

End of follow-up scratchpad. Will turn into a proper incident postmortem if SRE confirms root cause.
